records.name: Vaige
records.facts_used: Vaige is explained in the Estonian name collection through German ruhig and still, calm or quiet. The same entry compares it with Vaike. This directly connects the two spellings in a specific reference without requiring an invented, fixed direction of derivation between them. Julius Mägiste’s Eestipäraseid isikunimesid appeared in Tartu in 1929, with Vaige in its list of feminine names. This printed example establishes the form’s inclusion in a name collection of that period. The year dates the publication, not a proved invention or the naming of the first child.
records.reason: Exact-form origin or rendering evidence and a concrete historical, dictionary or professional episode support the five-language narrative.
records.uncertainties: Mägiste 1929 PDF p. 22 / printed p. 20 visually checked: feminine Vaige, gloss ruhig/still, explicit comparison with Vaike. Publisher confirms Julius Mägiste, Tartu 1929. Publication is not a coining or first-birth date; no unique direction of derivation is inferred.

records.name: Albertas
records.facts_used: Albertas is a Lithuanian name of Germanic origin. The guide gives its elements as adal, noble, and brecht, bright. These parts explain the historical structure of the name; they do not certify noble ancestry or a particular character for every present-day bearer. Lithuanian poet and translator Albertas Skyrelis supplies a concrete literary example of the name. The Writers’ Union bibliography dates his satirical poetry book Velnio tuzinas to 1977 and his lyric collection Pabūk džiaugsmu to 1987, documenting two distinct stages of his published work.
records.reason: Exact-form origin or rendering evidence and a concrete historical, dictionary or professional episode support the five-language narrative.
records.uncertainties: Exact LT-GUIDE gives adal/brecht. Directly opened Writers Union biography/bibliography confirms poet and translator Albertas Skyrelis, Velnio tuzinas 1977 and Pabūk džiaugsmu 1987.

records.name: Leopoldas
records.facts_used: Leopoldas is the Lithuanian rendering of Leopold, explicitly paired in the encyclopaedia’s entry on Emperor Leopold II. The family derives from Old German liut, people, and bald, bold or brave. A later association with Latin leo, lion, affected the spelling rather than supplying its original first element. In Lithuanian music history the name was borne by organist Leopoldas Digrys. The Academy of Music and Theatre’s departmental history records that his initiative reopened the organ class in 1962 after its closure in 1949, a specific contribution by a bearer to musical education.
records.reason: Exact-form origin or rendering evidence and a concrete historical, dictionary or professional episode support the five-language narrative.
records.uncertainties: VLE explicitly pairs Leopoldas II with Leopold II, supplying a rendering bridge to the curated liut/bald etymology. Directly opened LMTA history dates Leopoldas Digrys’s initiative to reopen the organ class to 1962, after closure in 1949. The popular guide says meaning still being clarified and its mixed similar-name list was not used. The inspected 1961 Latvian rendering manual p. 47 contains no Leopoldas pair.

records.name: Vaidilas
records.facts_used: The guide explains Vaidilas as a derivative of Vaidas, a shortening of names beginning Vaid-. This describes a route of personal-name formation. It does not by itself establish a connection with an ancient priestly title or a single literal translation of the whole name. In an essay on Lithuanian names, Antanas Salys contrasted the calendar form Vaidilis with the older Vaidilas, preferring the latter. The essay was reprinted in volume two of his writings in 1983. This documents a linguist’s discussion of the spelling rather than a claim that Vaidilas was created in 1983.
records.reason: Exact-form origin or rendering evidence and a concrete historical, dictionary or professional episode support the five-language narrative.
records.uncertainties: Exact LT-GUIDE derives Vaidilas from Vaidas, shortened from Vaid- names. Salys PDF p. 284 / printed p. 269 visually checked: essay prefers older Vaidilas over calendar Vaidilis. Checked publication is the 1983 collected volume, not an inferred original essay date. The p. 317 calendar instead has Vaidila (Vaidys), not this exact form.

records.name: Žadvydė
records.facts_used: Žadvydė is a Lithuanian feminine two-stem name. The guide explains žad- through žadėti, to intend or prepare, and vyd- through vydo, saw. These are explanations of individual elements, not sufficient grounds for one exact poetic translation of the whole name. A historical example of the family is the related masculine form Žadvydas. Volume two of Salys’s writings, published in 1983, includes it in a German–Lithuanian dictionary appendix as both a given name and a surname. This evidence concerns Žadvydas and does not date the first use of feminine Žadvydė.
records.reason: Exact-form origin or rendering evidence and a concrete historical, dictionary or professional episode support the five-language narrative.
records.uncertainties: LT-GUIDE explicitly gives a two-stem name, žadėti and (iš)vydo, with related Žadvyda/Žadvydas. Salys PDF p. 280 / printed p. 265 visually checked: Žadvydas as masculine given name and surname in a German–Lithuanian dictionary appendix. Narrative explicitly attributes this 1983 publication evidence to the related male form, not a first attestation or creation date of Žadvydė. No poetic whole-name translation, fictional bearer or company-name match was accepted.

records.name: Leopolds
records.facts_used: Leopolds combines Old High German liut, people, and bald, bold or brave, belonging to the same historical family as German Leopold. Association with Latin leo, lion, influenced the international spelling, but lion is not the original explanation of its first element. The Siliņš dictionary catalogue places a Leopolds record in Mazsalaca in the last quarter of the nineteenth century. It separately gives 1767 for calendar inclusion. The earlier calendar record and later evidence of personal use concern different kinds of sources, rather than a single date of invention.
records.reason: Exact-form origin or rendering evidence and a concrete historical, dictionary or professional episode support the five-language narrative.
records.uncertainties: LV-SILINS p. 213: liut/bald, Mazsalaca in the last quarter of the nineteenth century, calendar 1767. INT-BTN distinguishes the later leo spelling association from the original first element.

records.name: Unda
records.facts_used: The dictionary connects Unda with Latin unda, wave. This explanation concerns water imagery rather than personal character. The Latin word and the personal name explained through it belong to different periods: the age of the ancient word does not itself date the Latvian name’s formation. The catalogue records the personal name Unda in Riga in 1969, providing a specific place and time for this short form. Its entry supplies no calendar-inclusion year. The 1908 date in the Undīna/-e entry cannot be transferred to Unda, and the 1969 record does not prove there was no earlier use.
records.reason: Exact-form origin or rendering evidence and a concrete historical, dictionary or professional episode support the five-language narrative.
records.uncertainties: LV-SILINS p. 312: Latin unda, Riga 1969, no calendar-entry year. No 1908 transfer from the separate Undīna/-e entry.
